text:
jana-marketing: Quick experiment pitch: run a pricing page split that tests two things together this sprint — 1) tier naming frameworks (descriptive vs commitment-focused) and 2) a presets-based calculator (startup / growth / enterprise) that surfaces a webinar CTA when estimate > $3k/mo. Goal = see whether clearer names or preset scenarios drive higher calc->demo conversions.

 tom-growth: good. call the variants: V1 = "DescriptiveStacks" (names like 'Starter / Scale / Dedicated') V2 = "CommitFlex" (names like 'Pay-as-you-go / Committed / Enterprise'). also test CTA verb: 'Get estimate' vs 'See plan & price'. keep sample equal.

 alex-ux: UX constraints: keep presets visible as 3 buttons (startup/growth/enterprise) and allow manual edit after selection. avoid gating on first click. show a short line under result "Recommended for: <use case>" + two CTAs: 'Start trial' and 'Request demo'.

 jana-marketing: presets idea: prefill typical tokens/month + seq_len + concurrency so non-technical visitors get an immediate ballpark. capture email on demo request only, not on every calc interaction.

 alex-ux: rough presets json (for dev):
```
{
  "startup": {"monthly_tokens": 5e6, "seq_len": 512, "concurrency": 2},
  "growth": {"monthly_tokens": 5e7, "seq_len": 1024, "concurrency": 6},
  "enterprise": {"monthly_tokens": 5e8, "seq_len": 2048, "concurrency": 20}
}
```

 elaine-pd: FAQ microcopy plan: test compact accordion (one-liners) vs expanded (short paragraph). topics to cover: how charges accrue (tokens vs requests), committed vs burst behavior, what the calculator includes/excludes (e.g., embeddings, fine-tuning). sample one-liners: "Tokens are unit of use; caching and batching lower effective cost." and "Committed capacity gives predictable per-token economics and priority routing."

 nick-sales: routing rules: if estimate >= 3000 OR company_size in 150+ bucket => route to AE queue (nick-sales). For anything between 700-2999, mark as 'MQL' and queue to SDR. Include estimate_breakdown and preset_selected in lead notes.

 chris-analytics: event list I'll need: page_variant, preset_click, calc_edit, calc_submit, calc_estimate_value, demo_request, webinar_click, faq_expand_type. Also track channel (utm_source). Power calc: expect needing ~6k pv/week per variant to detect a 10% lift in calc->demo.

 jana-marketing: webinar tie-in: if estimate >= 3k offer 'fast-track webinar seat' CTA which asks for email + company_size and schedules into a 30-minute demo-prep webinar. growth-bot can handle scheduling.

 growth-bot: Note: tentative webinar slot available 2026-06-16 16:00 UTC. I can create a funnel for fast-track invites if enabled.

 tom-growth: timeline: build and QA this week, canary Mon, full run 10 days. primary success = lift in calc->demo of >=8%. secondary = webinar->demo conversion >=15%.

 alex-ux: accessibility note: ensure presets have ARIA labels and results table is screen-reader friendly. also include alt text for any tier icons.

 nick-sales: small ask: include a short 'deal trigger' flag if preset_selected == enterprise so AE can triage quickly.

 chris-analytics: I'll produce the event spec + sample size numbers by EOD tomorrow. please send any assumptions about baseline calc->demo rate.

 jana-marketing: baseline we have is ~0.9% calc->demo historically on pricing page. if that aligns with analytics we'll use it.

 tom-growth: I'll set up the experiment in Growthboard and create tickets for dev + copy. tagging @alex-ux @chris-analytics @nick-sales @elaine-pd.

 jana-marketing: next steps summary: alex -> prod-ready presets + accessibility tweaks, chris -> event spec + power calc, tom -> growthboard setup + tracking flags, nick -> SFDC mapping for estimate_breakdown & deal_trigger. I'll own copy and variant microcopy. Launch canary Mon and monitor for calc friction.

 nick-sales: will confirm SFDC field names & flow today.

 chris-analytics: will post the sample-size spreadsheet and event spec by 11am PT tomorrow.

 jana-marketing: thanks all. trying to keep this lightweight so we get clear signal fast. :seedling:
